activities.caption: run the 10% rule — what can the carnivores eat?
activities.name: ecoTenEstimate

config.prompt: Only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level reaches the next. A field carrying 1,000 kg of grass supports about 100 kg of herbivore — about how many kg of carnivore?
config.why: About 10 kg — the leak at every link (heat from respiration, uneaten parts, unabsorbed waste) is why big fierce animals are rare.
config.context: Measured transfers run roughly 5–20%; food chains rarely exceed four or five links because there is nothing left to eat the lion-eater.

activities.caption: true or false — what cycles, what leaks
activities.name: ecoCycleJudge

statements.s: Only matter cycles through ecosystems; energy is a one-way flow.
statements.why: Energy enters once as sunlight and leaves for space as infrared radiation — ecosystems need a continuous power supply.

statements.s: Decomposers add a trophic level of their own.
statements.why: Their job is releasing locked-up nutrients for producers to re-use — the return leg, not a rung.

statements.s: Heat lost during respiration can be harvested back into useful work by living things.
statements.why: That leak is precisely why only ~10% of energy survives each feeding step.

statements.s: Every ecosystem is two networks in one: energy flowing one way, matter cycling endlessly.
statements.why: The sun supplies the first; decomposers run the second.

activities.anchor: Webs show three things chains cannot
activities.caption: pair each web insight with its example
activities.name: ecoWebMatch

config.prompt: What food webs show that single chains cannot — pair them:

pairs.right: one prey collapse rarely starves a specialist

pairs.left: trophic position is a role, not a species
pairs.right: a fox eats berries and rabbits — two levels at once
count the organisms at each level

config.why: Numbers and biomass pyramids occasionally invert — one oak tree feeding thousands of aphids — but you cannot support more kilojoules of consumer than the producer level makes.

activities.anchor: the vegetation stores the equivalent of 100 million kilojoules
activities.caption: stack the hectare's energy budget
activities.name: ecoBudgetOrder

config.prompt: One hectare, one year, the 10% rule — put the budget in order:
items: Vegetation stores the equivalent of 100 million kilojoules a year
Primary carnivores get about a million
A top predator perhaps a hundred thousand
A few person-days of food energy from an entire hectare
config.why: That is the quantitative meaning of 'big fierce animals are rare' — and why a hectare of grain feeds far more humans than a hectare of grain-fed beef.

activities.caption: the carbon cycle's faucet — drag from past to present
activities.name: ecoCO2Compare

config.prompt: Atmospheric carbon dioxide — drag the divider across the industrial era:

before.label: pre-industrial
before.text: About 280 ppm — the carbon cycle's steady budget, with photosynthesis and respiration balanced.

after.label: today
after.text: Over 420 ppm — burning fossil carbon buried for hundreds of millions of years has opened an extra faucet.

config.why: Energy is a one-way river; matter is a closed loop — but the loop now runs with an extra faucet open.

activities.anchor: is the one with the most biology in
activities.caption: fill the blanks — unlocking the air's nitrogen
activities.name: ecoNitrogenCloze

config.text: Air is 78% nitrogen (N₂), but that triple-bonded molecule is unusable until %%0%% bacteria convert it to ammonium and nitrates plants can absorb. They live free in the soil — or housed in the %%1%% %%2%% of legumes such as beans and clover.
config.hint: The same bacteria are why farmers rotate beans and clover through their fields.

activities.caption: call the magnitude — St Matthew's boom
activities.name: ecoReindeerEstimate

config.prompt: 29 reindeer were released on St Matthew Island in 1944. Roughly how many were there by 1963, before the lichen ran out?
config.why: Over 6,000 by 1963 — then the lichen ran out and only tens of survivors remained by 1966. Overshoot crashes; K also moves: the reindeer crashed their own carrying capacity.
config.context: A population that overshoots the limit is this lesson's cautionary worked example.

activities.anchor: rise and fall together, roughly every decade
activities.caption: rebuild the predator–prey oscillator
activities.name: ecoLynxOrder

config.prompt: A century of Hudson Bay fur records, one loop — put the cycle in order:
items: Hare numbers rise again — the lynx peak lagging a year or two behind
config.why: A predator–prey oscillator built from nothing but birth and death rates — the lagged chase Gause reproduced in laboratory vessels.
